## Description

Primary source:

<https://ngs101.com/how-to-analyze-single-cell-rna-seq-data-complete-beginners-guide-part-4-cell-type-identification/>

Part 1 of 3. Clusters from tutorial 3 are given biological identities by
inspecting canonical marker genes and data-driven cluster markers, then
assigning a manual label to each cluster. Parts 2 and 3 add automated
annotation (SingleR, scType, scCATCH) and compare the methods.

Code here follows the structure and settings described in the source article but
was written for this notebook series (parameters pulled into the YAML front
matter; paths built from `params`).

## Libraries and directories

```{r step1_libs_data}

# Core single-cell analysis
library(Seurat)              # Main scRNA-seq toolkit
library(SeuratObject)        # Seurat object infrastructure

# Visualization and data manipulation
library(ggplot2)             # Custom plots when needed
library(patchwork)           # Combine plots
library(dplyr)               # Data manipulation
library(scales)              # Plot scales
library(viridis)             # Color palettes

if (!exists("params") || !is.list(params)) {
  # Running interactively (e.g. via "Run Cell") rather than through
  # knit/render, so `params` was never created by rmarkdown::render().
  # Reconstruct it by parsing this .Rmd's own YAML header, so the params
  # defaults live in exactly one place (the YAML block above) instead of
  # being duplicated here.
  rmd_path <- tryCatch(
    # Only reliable when this document is the active editor tab; if focus
    # has moved to another file, this will pick up the wrong path.
    rstudioapi::getSourceEditorContext()$path,
    error = function(e) NA_character_
  )
  if (is.na(rmd_path) || !nzchar(rmd_path)) {
    # Fallback if rstudioapi is unavailable or no doc is focused; assumes
    # the working directory is the project root.
    rmd_path <- "scRNAseq_tutorial_4_cell_type_annotation/tut4_cell_type_annotation_part1.Rmd"
  }
  params <- rmarkdown::yaml_front_matter(rmd_path)$params
}

# Set working directory
base.dir <- params$base.dir
annot.dir <- file.path(base.dir, params$annot.subdir)

# Create output directories
for (d in c("plots/manual_annotation", "annotations")) {
  if (!dir.exists(file.path(annot.dir, d))) dir.create(file.path(annot.dir, d), recursive = TRUE)
}

# Set random seed for reproducibility
set.seed(params$seed)

# Configure plotting defaults
theme_set(theme_classic(base_size = 12))

# Column names and colors from params
cluster.col <- params$cluster.col
sample.col <- params$sample.col
condition.col <- params$condition.col
condition.colors <- setNames(unlist(params$condition.palette), unlist(params$condition.levels))

# Intermediate file passed on to part 2
annotated_part1.file <- "integrated_manual_annotated_seurat.rds"
```

## Load integrated Seurat object from tutorial 3

```{r step2_load_obj}
integrated.file <- file.path(base.dir, params$integrated.rds)
cat("Reading in integrated Seurat object:", integrated.file, "\n")
integrated_seurat <- readRDS(integrated.file)

cat("Cells:", ncol(integrated_seurat), " Genes:", nrow(integrated_seurat), "\n")
cat("Assays:", paste(Assays(integrated_seurat), collapse = ", "), "\n")
cat("Reductions:", paste(Reductions(integrated_seurat), collapse = ", "), "\n")

stopifnot(cluster.col %in% colnames(integrated_seurat@meta.data))

# Choose the first UMAP reduction from the priority list that is present
umap_reduction <- intersect(params$umap.priority, Reductions(integrated_seurat))[1]
if (is.na(umap_reduction)) stop("None of params$umap.priority found in object reductions")
cat("Using UMAP reduction:", umap_reduction, "\n")
```

### Starting point: clusters, samples, conditions

```{r step3_start_plots, fig.width = 14, fig.height = 10}
p1 <- DimPlot(integrated_seurat, reduction = umap_reduction, group.by = cluster.col,
              label = TRUE, label.size = 5, pt.size = 0.1) + ggtitle("Clusters")
p2 <- DimPlot(integrated_seurat, reduction = umap_reduction, group.by = sample.col,
              pt.size = 0.1) + ggtitle("Samples")
p3 <- DimPlot(integrated_seurat, reduction = umap_reduction, group.by = condition.col,
              pt.size = 0.1) +
  scale_color_manual(values = condition.colors) + ggtitle("Condition")

p_overview <- (p1 | p2) / (p3 | plot_spacer())
print(p_overview)
ggsave(file.path(annot.dir, "plots/00_starting_clusters.png"), p_overview,
       width = 14, height = 10, dpi = params$plot.dpi)
```

## Normalize and scale the RNA assay

Marker visualization and differential expression need log-normalized data and
scaled values for heatmaps. Tutorial 3 may have left the object with split
layers and `SCT` as the default assay, so the `RNA` assay is joined and
normalized explicitly here.

```{r step4_normalize}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 1: Log-normalize and scale the RNA assay
#-----------------------------------------------

DefaultAssay(integrated_seurat) <- "RNA"

# Seurat v5: merge per-sample layers into single counts/data layers
integrated_seurat <- JoinLayers(integrated_seurat)

integrated_seurat <- NormalizeData(integrated_seurat,
                                   normalization.method = "LogNormalize",
                                   scale.factor = params$norm.scale.factor,
                                   verbose = FALSE)
integrated_seurat <- ScaleData(integrated_seurat,
                               features = rownames(integrated_seurat),
                               verbose = FALSE)

Idents(integrated_seurat) <- cluster.col
```

## Manual annotation: canonical marker genes

Single markers are rarely sufficient; each cell type is checked against a small
panel. This PBMC panel is specific to the example dataset (edit for other
tissues).

```{r step5_canonical_markers}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 2: Canonical marker panel
#-----------------------------------------------

canonical_markers <- list(
  "T_cells"            = c("CD3D", "CD3E", "CD3G"),
  "CD4_T"              = c("CD3D", "CD4", "IL7R"),
  "CD8_T"              = c("CD3D", "CD8A", "CD8B"),
  "B_cells"            = c("CD79A", "MS4A1", "CD19"),
  "NK_cells"           = c("NKG7", "GNLY", "NCAM1"),
  "Monocytes"          = c("CD14", "LYZ", "S100A8", "S100A9"),
  "Classical_Mono"     = c("CD14", "S100A8", "FCGR3A"),
  "Non_Classical_Mono" = c("FCGR3A", "MS4A7"),
  "Dendritic_cells"    = c("FCER1A", "CST3"),
  "Plasmacytoid_DC"    = c("IL3RA", "GZMB", "SERPINF1"),
  "Platelets"          = c("PPBP", "PF4", "GP9")
)

# Which markers are present in the object?
all_genes <- rownames(integrated_seurat)
canonical_present <- lapply(canonical_markers, function(g) g[g %in% all_genes])
for (ct in names(canonical_markers)) {
  cat(sprintf("%-20s %d/%d markers present\n", ct,
              length(canonical_present[[ct]]), length(canonical_markers[[ct]])))
}
all_markers_present <- unique(unlist(canonical_present))
```

```{r step6_marker_plot_functions}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 3: Helper functions for marker visualization
#-----------------------------------------------

plot_violin_markers <- function(obj, genes, suffix) {
  if (length(genes) == 0) return(invisible(NULL))
  p <- VlnPlot(obj, features = genes, group.by = cluster.col, pt.size = 0, ncol = 3)
  ggsave(file.path(annot.dir, "plots/manual_annotation", paste0("violin_", suffix, ".png")),
         p, width = 14, height = 4 * ceiling(length(genes) / 3), dpi = params$plot.dpi)
  p
}

plot_umap_markers <- function(obj, genes, suffix) {
  if (length(genes) == 0) return(invisible(NULL))
  p <- FeaturePlot(obj, features = genes, reduction = umap_reduction, ncol = 4, pt.size = 0.1)
  ggsave(file.path(annot.dir, "plots/manual_annotation", paste0("umap_", suffix, ".png")),
         p, width = 16, height = 4 * ceiling(length(genes) / 4), dpi = params$plot.dpi)
  p
}
```

### Dot plot of all canonical markers

```{r step7_dotplot, fig.width = 12, fig.height = 10}
p_dot <- DotPlot(integrated_seurat, features = all_markers_present,
                 group.by = cluster.col) + coord_flip()
print(p_dot)
ggsave(file.path(annot.dir, "plots/manual_annotation/dotplot_all_canonical_markers.png"),
       p_dot, width = 12, height = 10, dpi = params$plot.dpi)
```

### Violin and UMAP plots by lineage

```{r step8_lineage_plots, fig.width = 14, fig.height = 8}
for (ct in names(canonical_present)) {
  print(plot_violin_markers(integrated_seurat, canonical_present[[ct]], ct))
  print(plot_umap_markers(integrated_seurat, canonical_present[[ct]], ct))
}
```

## Manual annotation: data-driven cluster markers

```{r step9_findallmarkers}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 4: Find markers for every cluster
#-----------------------------------------------

# Exclude mitochondrial and ribosomal genes, species-dependent
if (params$species == "human") {
  exclude_regex <- "^RP[SL]|^MT-"
} else if (params$species == "mouse") {
  exclude_regex <- "^Rp[sl]|^mt-"
} else {
  stop("params$species must be 'human' or 'mouse'")
}

cluster_markers <- FindAllMarkers(integrated_seurat,
                                  only.pos = TRUE,
                                  min.pct = params$markers.min_pct,
                                  logfc.threshold = params$markers.logfc,
                                  verbose = FALSE)

cluster_markers_filtered <- cluster_markers %>%
  filter(!grepl(exclude_regex, gene))

top_markers <- cluster_markers_filtered %>%
  group_by(cluster) %>%
  slice_max(order_by = avg_log2FC, n = params$markers.top_n) %>%
  arrange(cluster, desc(avg_log2FC))

write.csv(cluster_markers, file.path(annot.dir, "annotations/cluster_markers_all.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(top_markers, file.path(annot.dir, "annotations/top_markers_per_cluster.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)

print(as.data.frame(top_markers), row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r step10_heatmap, fig.width = 12, fig.height = 14}
top_genes <- unique(top_markers$gene)
p_heatmap <- DoHeatmap(integrated_seurat, features = top_genes,
                       group.by = cluster.col, size = 3)
print(p_heatmap)
ggsave(file.path(annot.dir, "plots/manual_annotation/heatmap_top_markers.png"),
       p_heatmap, width = 12, height = 14, dpi = params$plot.dpi)
```

## Manual annotation: assign cluster identities

**The mapping below is the source article's example for GSE174609 and must be
checked against the dot plot, violin plots and marker tables above for any new
run (different clustering resolution = different cluster numbers).**

```{r step11_manual_mapping, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 6}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 5: Cluster -> cell type mapping (EDIT FOR YOUR DATA)
#-----------------------------------------------

cluster_to_celltype <- c(
  "0"  = "CD4+ T cells",  "1"  = "CD4+ T cells", "2"  = "NK cells",
  "3"  = "NK cells",      "4"  = "CD4+ T cells", "5"  = "NK cells",
  "6"  = "Classical Mono", "7" = "B Cells",      "8"  = "CD8+ T Cells",
  "9"  = "B Cells",       "10" = "CD4+ T cells", "11" = "CD4+ T cells",
  "12" = "Monocytes",     "13" = "CD4+ T cells", "14" = "NK cells",
  "15" = "NK cells",      "16" = "Platelets"
)

cluster_ids <- as.character(integrated_seurat@meta.data[[cluster.col]])
missing_clusters <- setdiff(unique(cluster_ids), names(cluster_to_celltype))
if (length(missing_clusters) > 0) {
  warning("Clusters without a manual label: ", paste(missing_clusters, collapse = ", "))
}

integrated_seurat$manual_annotation <- unname(cluster_to_celltype[cluster_ids])

print(table(integrated_seurat$manual_annotation, useNA = "ifany"))

p_manual <- DimPlot(integrated_seurat, reduction = umap_reduction,
                    group.by = "manual_annotation", label = TRUE, repel = TRUE,
                    pt.size = 0.1) + ggtitle("Manual annotation")
print(p_manual)
ggsave(file.path(annot.dir, "plots/manual_annotation/umap_manual_annotation.png"),
       p_manual, width = 9, height = 7, dpi = params$plot.dpi)
```

## Save object for part 2

```{r step12_save}
saveRDS(integrated_seurat, file.path(annot.dir, "annotations", annotated_part1.file))
save(umap_reduction, cluster_to_celltype,
     file = file.path(annot.dir, "annotations", "annot_part1.RData"))
```
